seo_title: Delhi HC Orders Amazon Takedown of Fake Alps Goods
title: Delhi HC Restrains Amazon Sellers of Counterfeit Alps Goodness Rosemary Water
case_name: Manash Lifestyle Private Limited v. Mayur Dhanji Hanat & Ors.
citation: CS(COMM) 1180/2026, Delhi High Court, ex parte interim order dated 2 November 2026 (Vikas Mahajan, J.)
card_summary: The Delhi High Court, on an ex parte application by Manash Lifestyle Private Limited, which runs Purplle, restrained two Amazon sellers, Zelta Enterprises and Diya Enterprises Gallery, from selling counterfeit Alps Goodness products, including its Rosemary Water. Justice Vikas Mahajan directed Amazon to take down the listings and disclose the sellers' KYC and GST details, leaving genuine listings untouched.
card_tip: A brand owner that finds counterfeit listings on Amazon can seek an ex parte order directing the platform to delist them and hand over the seller's KYC and GST details, without disturbing genuine sellers' listings.
verification_notes: AUDIENCE: domestic (an Indian personal care brand and its authorised sellers), with a secondary HNI/promoter angle for owners protecting a company's mark online. TARGET QUERY: how to stop counterfeit sellers on Amazon in India. DEMAND EVIDENCE: none seen. Cross-verified across LiveLaw Biz and BananaIP, which agree on the parties (Manash Lifestyle Private Limited as plaintiff; Mayur Dhanji Hanat, Zelta Enterprises, Diya Enterprises Gallery and Amazon Seller Services Private Limited as defendants), the case number (CS(COMM) 1180/2026), the 2 November 2026 date of the order, Justice Vikas Mahajan as the bench, the counterfeit Alps Goodness Rosemary Water allegation, and the direction to Amazon to take down the identified listings and disclose seller KYC/GST details while leaving genuine listings in place. This is an interim order, not a final decree, and the card states it as such.
